title: Law student charged after military-grade bomb intercepted near Irish border
excerpt: Isobella Perrie Sullivan, 25, remanded in custody after intelligence-led operation against dissident republicans
content_html:
A 25-year-old law student has been charged in relation to an “extremely significant” bomb intercepted near the UK-Irish border.

Isobella Perrie Sullivan, from Clane, County Kildare, was charged with possession of explosives at a special sitting of Trim district court on Friday evening.

Garda Síochána said in a statement that a second person, a man in his 40s arrested in connection with the investigation, remained detained in relation to offences against the state.

Both were arrested after police in Ireland targeting dissident republicans intercepted a vehicle that was allegedly transporting the device, after receiving intelligence information, police said.

Members of the Garda Síochána’s special detective unit stopped the vehicle travelling on the N2 south of Carrickmacross, County Monaghan, on Wednesday afternoon

Revealing details of the interception on Friday, Garda sources said the bomb was “highly sophisticated”, had been completed and was ready for use. It contained a power unit, a detonator and military-grade explosives they believed to be semtex.

Security sources said the probable intended use was as an under-car explosive for an attack in Northern Ireland.

Gardaí requested the assistance of the Irish Defence Forces explosive ordnance disposal team, which completed an examination of the vehicle south of Carrickmacross.

The Garda commissioner, Justin Kelly, confirmed details of the operation as he spoke to media at a Garda graduation event in County Tipperary on Friday.

“To be clear, what we found was an extremely significant seizure,” he said. “So this was an explosive device.

“Any seizure of this nature is really concerning. However, we certainly know that there are a small minority of dissident republicans who did not agree with the Good Friday agreement, they did not put weapons and explosives [out of use], they didn’t, you know, go through with the proper process in relation to decommissioning. So that is something that we continue to deal with.”

Kelly added: “There’s a small minority of these individuals, I would describe them as radicalised republicans, and this is a threat that we’re going to continue to face for some time in An Garda Síochána.

“But what I will say, certainly, it was a significant explosive device. So certainly not just the seizure of components or pieces. This was an explosive device and it would have or could have potentially caused significant damage.”

The commissioner confirmed the operation relied on intelligence. “Obviously, this was not a random stop,” Kelly said. “This is an intelligence-led operation, so we certainly do have information in relation to the individuals involved.”

A security source said the fact a bomb of that nature had been built and transported to the border was worrying because of the level of skill involved. It required mechanical and electrical knowledge and the sourcing of explosives.

They said that “radicalisation of individuals captured by the internet” meant individuals, rather than organised networks, could be at the centre of the incident.

Pipe bombs that have been used in the recent past to target members of the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) can be “relatively crude” but this bomb appeared to be different and would have needed an initiating device and a timer.

The fact that the Garda intercepted the bomb showed its intelligence gathering was working. However, the incident will fuel concerns about the level of counter-terrorism resourcing since the 1998 peace deal.

Kelly said: “We work very closely with our colleagues in PSNI and the intelligence services in the UK to deal with this threat. But I want to commend the members of An Garda Síochána who are involved in this operation.”

Perrie Sullivan was remanded in custody until a bail hearing on Monday. Bail would only be granted under a series of strict conditions.

content_html_zh:
一名 25 岁的法学院学生因在英国和爱尔兰边境附近截获的一枚“极其重要”的炸弹而受到指控。

来自基尔代尔郡克莱恩的伊莎贝拉·佩里·沙利文 (Isobella Perrie Sullivan) 于周五晚上在特里姆地区法院的一次特别会议上被指控持有爆炸物。

Garda Síochána 在一份声明中表示，另一名男子，一名因调查而被捕的 40 多岁男子，因涉嫌危害国家罪而仍被拘留。

警方表示，爱尔兰警方在收到情报后拦截了一辆据称运输该设备的车辆，针对持不同政见的共和党人，两人均被捕。

周三下午，爱尔兰警察特别侦探小组的成员在莫纳汉郡卡里克马克罗斯以南的 N2 公路上拦截了这辆车辆

警方消息人士在周五透露了拦截的细节时表示，这枚炸弹“高度复杂”，已经完成并准备使用。 它包含一个动力装置、一个雷管和他们认为是 semtex 的军用级炸药。

安全部门消息人士称，其可能的用途是作为北爱尔兰袭击事件中的车下炸药。

警察请求爱尔兰国防军爆炸物处理小组提供协助，该小组完成了对卡里克麦克罗斯以南车辆的检查。

周五，警察局长贾斯汀·凯利在蒂珀雷里郡举行的警察毕业典礼上向媒体发表讲话时证实了此次行动的细节。

“需要明确的是，我们发现的是一次极其严重的癫痫发作，”他说。 “所以这是一个爆炸装置。

“任何这种性质的扣押都非常令人担忧。 然而，我们当然知道有一小部分持不同政见的共和党人不同意耶稣受难日协议，他们没有停止使用武器和爆炸物，你知道，他们没有完成与退役有关的适当程序。 所以这是我们继续处理的事情。”

凯利补充道：“这些人中只有一小部分，我将他们描述为激进的共和党人，这是我们在爱尔兰警察局将在一段时间内继续面临的威胁。

“但我要说的是，当然，这是一个重要的爆炸装置。 因此，当然不仅仅是扣押零部件。 这是一个爆炸装置，它已经或可能已经造成重大损害。”

专员证实该行动依赖于情报。 “显然，这不是随机停留，”凯利说。 “这是一次以情报为主导的行动，因此我们当然掌握与所涉个人有关的信息。”

一名安全消息人士表示，这种性质的炸弹已被制造出来并运到边境，这一事实令人担忧，因为涉及的技术水平很高。 它需要机械和电气知识以及炸药的采购。

他们表示，“互联网捕获的个人的激进化”意味着个人，而不是有组织的网络，可能成为事件的中心。

最近用于针对北爱尔兰警察局（PSNI）成员的管状炸弹可能“相对粗糙”，但这种炸弹似乎有所不同，需要一个启动装置和一个计时器。

警察拦截炸弹的事实表明其情报收集工作正在发挥作用。 然而，这一事件将加剧人们对 1998 年和平协议以来反恐资源水平的担忧。

凯利说：“我们与 PSNI 的同事以及英国情报部门密切合作，应对这一威胁。 但我要赞扬参与这次行动的爱尔兰警察局成员。”

佩里·沙利文 (Perrie Sullivan) 被还押候审，直至周一举行保释听证会。 只有在一系列严格的条件下才能获得保释。
